summary: Blog article (not a case study) from Silver Oak Capital on how a property developer should choose a development finance broker / property finance specialist. Thesis [b]: property development finance is complex, so picking the right intermediary matters; a broker assesses the project and connects the developer with lenders offering competitive terms, including lenders the developer could not approach directly. Concrete guidance [a]: (1) Lender network - the broker should have connections with a diverse range of lenders, including specialist funding such as bridging loans and structured development finance, so the developer has multiple funding options to compare. (2) Fees - scrutinise the fee structure; typical figures cited: application fee around GBP 1,500, success fee of 0.5% at offer and 0.5% at completion, lender fees generally around 2%, with exit, valuation and legal costs possibly applying on top; a trustworthy broker is upfront about all costs. (3) Reputation - check client testimonials, reviews and case studies to gauge credibility. (4) Communication - approvals can take a long time, so clear and prompt communication is a key criterion. The search tool noted the piece is broker marketing favouring brokers in general and Silver Oak specifically, and that its figures are typical ranges, not quoted terms. Page age per search metadata: about 212 days / roughly seven months before 2026-10-29 (i.e. approximately late March 2026).
